title: Telecommunications and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2025
short_title: Telecommunications and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change telecommunications interception and criminal procedure laws governing network warrant information, capability testing, international production orders and authorisation of controlled police operations.
Network warrant information could be disclosed to meet prosecution duties and admitted for a defendant's fair trial, with prosecution evidence allowed in response to defence evidence.
Stored communications could be accessed under development and testing authorisations, with information use confined to those purposes and subject to the interception framework's safeguards.
changes: The Communications Access Coordinator role would move to the secretary of the department administering interception law, identified in the source as Home Affairs.
Communications providers could comply with relevant interception production orders by supplying copies of stored communications.
Security authorities would have to destroy stored communications information obtained through testing authorisations as soon as practicable.
Controlled-operation safety assessments would focus on direct, reasonably foreseeable consequences of participants' unlawful conduct.
summary.affected: Law enforcement and security agencies, telecommunications providers, prosecutors, defendants and officials administering interception authorisations are affected.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of the Telecommunications and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2025, arguing that it would clarify surveillance, interception, international production orders and controlled operations frameworks. The bill would support access to certain stored communications, strengthen safeguards and assist investigations of serious online crime, including child exploitation, while retaining strict controls.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Wallace
speeches.brief: Presented reports supporting the listing of Terrorgram as a terrorist organisation under the Criminal Code and recommending passage without amendment of the Telecommunications and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2025, which makes technical changes to telecommunications, surveillance and criminal justice laws.
